subject: Velociti renewal and capacity recast — proposed commit, rateband smoothing
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara@velociti.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal — commit uplift + rate smoothing (Velociti)

Hi Sara,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our conversation, attached is a concise renewal proposal that moves Velociti from your current hosted tier to a 12‑month committed plan that better fits your seasonal peak and smoothing needs. High level:

- Monthly commit: 2.25M tokens (up from 1.2M)
- Effective per‑token rate: $0.0018 (10% reduction vs current over 12 months)
- Soft throttle / smoothing: committed baseline with a 20% burst pocket and automatic smoothing across the month to avoid short‑duration throttles
- Burst credits: 50k tokens per month to handle spikes (applies before overage)
- SLA: 99.9% availability for our hosted API endpoints; proposed SLA addendum attached as draft

Attachments: Velociti_Renewal_Proposal_20260909.pdf, SLA_Addendum_Draft.docx

Next steps I recommend:
1) Procurement review of the proposal and legal review of the SLA addendum (if you want changes, flag them).
2) Ops onboarding call (we can schedule with Marissa and Stephanie) to set smoothing windows and burst plumbing.
3) Sign and return to get the new commit in place by Oct 1 to cover your Q4 ramp.

If you want a shorter ramp, we can layer a stepped commit (2 months at 1.5M, then full 2.25M). We can also offer a 30‑day performance review with rollback triggers if latency/regression concerns appear.

Open to a quick call today or tomorrow to walk procurement through the doc.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai | +1 415‑555‑0123

---

From: Sara Liu <sara@velociti.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@velociti.ai>, Mark D'Souza <mdsouza@velociti.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal — commit uplift + rate smoothing (Velociti)

Karthik —

Appreciate the clear proposal. This direction makes sense to support our Q4 traffic. A couple quick asks from procurement/legal:

- Can you confirm whether the 20% burst pocket is billable immediately after depletion or whether there's a grace window?
- We prefer a 30‑day ramp to the full commit over a stepped 2‑month approach — is that supported?
- Can you provide a one‑page summary for our finance team showing monthly cost at committed vs 10% overage?

Looping Mark from Legal and procurement for visibility. Procurement will push for net‑30 payment terms (we typically do net‑30 for renewals).

I’ll review the SLA addendum and come back with redlines. Can you also confirm start date options (Oct 1 vs Oct 15)?

Thanks,
Sara
Head of Product Operations | Velociti.ai
sara@velociti.ai

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara@velociti.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Mark D'Souza <mdsouza@velociti.ai>, Procurement <procurement@velociti.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal — commit uplift + rate smoothing (Velociti)

Sara — thanks. Quick answers:

- Burst pocket behavior: burst credits are consumed first and are not billable; once the burst pool is exhausted, usage falls back to the committed baseline and overages apply at the overage rate in the proposal. We can include an additional 7‑day grace buffer on first month if you want to avoid an immediate overage charge while you calibrate.
- 30‑day ramp: yes, we support a 30‑day ramp (start at 1.4M for 30 days, then full 2.25M). I’ll update the proposal to show the stepped ramp as an option.
- Cost one‑pager: attached as the first two pages of the proposal PDF; happy to extract to a separate summary if procurement prefers a single sheet.
- Start date: Oct 1 or Oct 15 both work; to lock pricing we recommend sign by Sept 24.

Also, as an incentive for a 12‑month commit we can provide a 10% discount (already reflected in the effective per‑token rate) and a one‑time onboarding credit worth $5k for usage during the first 60 days. If procurement needs a more formal concession, let me know and I’ll escalate.

Marissa / Stephanie — can you confirm operational plan below and whether the SLA addendum requires any high‑touch support for the first 30 days?

Thanks,
Karthik

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Liu <sara@velociti.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal proposal — commit uplift + rate smoothing (Velociti)

Karthik — quick ops note for the thread.

We can support the 30‑day ramp and the burst pocket semantics as described. Operational checklist:
- Pre‑sign: confirm source IPs and VPC peering window (if they opt for private peering).
- Day 0 (start): enable smoothing policy with 24h lookback, provision commit in billing, seed KV cache for anticipated heavy prefixes.
- Day 7: burst behavior review — compare actual token burn to expected and adjust soft throttle thresholds if needed.
- Day 30: performance review and SLA KPI check; if >2x observed latency on minority of routes, we trigger the rollback clause in the configuration doc.

Question for legal/procurement (cc'd): what are Velociti's preferred invoice cadence? Karthik mentioned monthly billing by default; procurement sometimes requests net‑30 with consolidated quarterly statements.

Happy to run the ops onboarding call next week — suggest Wed 16 Sept at 09:00 PT.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

---

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sara Liu <sara@velociti.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:17:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal proposal — commit uplift + rate smoothing (Velociti)

Sara / team — technical confirmation and recommended config for the proposed commit: 

- Recommended model: redwood-l2-3b-q4 (best perf/cost for Velociti's 1–2s caption path).
- Batch window: start with 30ms aggregation for foreground traffic, ramp to 50ms if latency headroom observed.
- KV cache prewarm: we will preseed hot keys for the top 25 prefixes you provided in the last SOW.
- Soft throttle thresholds: recommend baseline at 100% commit, soft throttle at 120% sustained for >60s before shedding to priority lanes; this aligns with the 20% burst pocket.

Attachment: SLA_Addendum_Draft.docx (updated with our suggested metric clarifications in the latency section).

I'll join the ops onboarding call and prepare a short runbook for your infra team. If you want, I can also include a short test plan we will run during Day 0 to ensure perf and token accounting match.

-Stephanie
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.ai

---

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Sara Liu <sara@velociti.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Approval to finalize concession and proceed to contract (Velociti / DEAL-2026-0457)

Team / Sara — quick note from sales leadership. Karthik, approve the 10% concession for a 12‑month commit and the $5k onboarding credit. Work with procurement on net‑30 if they require it, but prioritize signing by 24 Sept to lock pricing. Marissa, please own the ops onboarding timeline and ensure the Day 7 review is scheduled. Stephanie, finalize the SLA addendum and attach to the DocuSign.

Velociti — thanks for moving quickly. Once procurement confirms net terms and signatory, we’ll push the contract to DocuSign under DEAL-2026-0457 and target an Oct 1 kickoff (30‑day ramp available on request).

Rishi Malhotra
VP Sales | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai
